correctness.rationale: Every shortest-path normalized molecule is the average of oriented edge molecules, so edges norm any operator. An extreme normalized dual Lipschitz potential has a spanning connected tight-edge graph; otherwise a slack component could be shifted in both directions. Tight differences are \(\pm1\), forcing integral vertex values. At a neutral edge \(h(a)=h(b)\), directed costs \(c(s,t)=1+\min(0,h(t)-h(s))\in\{0,1\}\) give distance \(g(b)=0,g(a)=1\): zero-cost paths lower the integer potential strictly and cannot connect equal heights. Forward and reverse triangle inequalities imply both \(g\) and \(h-g\) are 1-Lipschitz. Normalized components norm the chosen edge with opposite signs; thus \(|h(Tm)|\le2v(T)\), and extremal dual evaluation yields the global norm inequality. The equilateral triangle equality follows from Cobollo--Guirao--Montesinos, Corollary 5.3. Independently reproduced the shortest-path splitting for all 771 labeled connected graphs on 2--5 vertices, 41,463 integer Lipschitz potentials, and 88,156 neutral-edge incidences; this finite test is corroboration only.
correctness.risk: Graph connectivity, unit edges, finite-dimensional dual-polytope extreme points, and real scalars are essential; the finite enumeration alone cannot establish the all-graphs bound.

final_claim: For every finite connected simple unit-edge graph \(G\) on at least two vertices, the real Lipschitz-free space \(\mathcal F(V(G))\) has \(1/2\le n(\mathcal F(V(G)))\le1\), equivalently \(\|T\|\le2v(T)\) for each operator; the constant is sharp at \(K_3\).
limitations: Real scalars, finite connected simple graphs with every edge length one only.
Does not extend to arbitrary weighted graphs, infinite graphs or complex free spaces.
This is a uniform bound, not an exact numerical index for every nonbipartite graph.
